To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the simulation of the seismic-wave propagation of the 2011 earthquake is successfully performed by using a 3D heterogeneous structure model and a high-performance computing system; (b) the simulated wave-field exhibits a strongly complex pattern, reflecting both the source complexity and heterogeneities around and below the source region; (c) the simulated wavefield is in good agreement with observed seismograms, and the simulated waveforms can be used for the estimation of the source mechanism of the earthquake.
the 3D structure and the source complexity play a key role in generating the complex pattern of the seismic waves.
the 3D simulation of the wave-field for the 2011 M9 earthquake is feasible by using multi-GPUs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a large-scale simulation for a realistic 3D structure.
the development of a numerical method for the simulation of seismic-wave propagation in a large-scale heterogeneous medium, and with its application to the 2011 M 9.0 Tohoku-Ohi earthquake.
the development of a large-scale simulation system for earthquake ground motion and tsunami propagation.
